transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning and welcome to S-Net customer technical support, my name is Mark. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Mark. Our S-Net TV 360 box keeps freezing whenever we open Netflix or Prime Video, and when it does play, the picture is stuck in blurry low definition instead of 4K HDR.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how annoying it is when streaming apps buffer and fail to display in full 4K HDR, Elijah. I will check your video output and bandwidth settings to get this sorted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Mark. We pay for the Ultra HD tier and it looks like standard definition right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we run diagnostics on the TV 360 box, Elijah, could you verify your full home address and your four-digit security PIN for me?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 88 Langdale Court, Carlisle, CA1 3TY, and the PIN is 7194.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Elijah. I have your TV 360 entertainment profile open in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you are experiencing: your TV 360 streaming apps are buffering and failing to render in 4K HDR, while the picture drops to standard definition during playback. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. It happens on both Netflix and Prime Video, and sometimes the screen goes black for three seconds like it's losing connection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When the screen goes black momentarily on 4K content, it usually points to an HDCP 2.2 digital handshake failure between the TV box and your television HDMI port.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does HDCP mean?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection is the encryption handshake required for 4K streaming. If the HDMI port or cable cannot maintain HDCP 2.2 sync, the app forces a fallback to low definition.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We have the HDMI cable plugged into HDMI port three on our Samsung television.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On many Samsung smart televisions, only HDMI port one or port two supports full HDMI 2.0 with HDCP 2.2 and Enhanced Color.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh really? I didn't realize different ports had different capabilities.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you check the labels on the back of your television set? Is HDMI port one labeled as Enhanced or 4K 60Hz?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look behind the TV... yes! Port one says eARC and 4K 60Hz, while port three just says standard HDMI.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's move the high-speed HDMI cable from port three into HDMI port one while the box is on standby.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Switching the cable to port one now... okay, clicked firmly into port one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now turn the television back on and switch the source input to HDMI one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Switching input to HDMI one... the S-Net TV 360 home screen popped up immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On your Samsung TV remote, open Settings, General, External Device Manager, and turn on HDMI UHD Color for port one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Navigating to External Device Manager... turning on Input Signal Plus for HDMI one... okay, the TV flashed and reloaded.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now on the S-Net 360 remote, press Home, go to Settings, then Audio and Video, then Video Resolution.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening Video Resolution... it was on 1080p automatic, but now 2160p 4K HDR is available as an option!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Select 2160p 4K HDR and press OK to lock the display output.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Selecting 2160p... the screen refreshed and says 4K HDR Active with 10-bit color depth!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's check your broadband speed to the TV 360 box. Is the box connected via Wi-Fi or an Ethernet cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's connected via Wi-Fi to our S-Net Hub in the hallway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On the TV 360 Network menu, what download speed is the box reporting under Network Diagnostics?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Testing connection... it says link speed is one hundred and eighty megabits on five gigahertz.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: One hundred and eighty megabits is more than seven times the twenty-five megabits required for seamless 4K HDR streaming.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's plenty of bandwidth then.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What about audio settings? Do you have an external soundbar connected to the eARC port?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We have a Sonos Beam soundbar connected to the optical port.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In that case, in Audio Settings on the 360 box, ensure Dolby Audio is set to Dolby Digital Plus pass-through.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Setting Dolby Digital Plus... the soundbar just chirped to indicate surround sound ready.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the TV 360 box support Dolby Atmos audio over the HDMI eARC connection to our soundbar?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, in the Audio Output settings, selecting Dolby Digital Plus with Atmos pass-through enables full Dolby Atmos height spatial audio on compatible Netflix and Prime Video titles.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I see the Dolby Atmos logo showing up on our soundbar display right now, that sounds incredible!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms uncompressed audio bitstreaming is fully synchronized alongside your 4K video.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The sound separation across the living room is noticeably richer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about two minutes while I clear the application cache on your TV box from our server console.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Elijah. The streaming app cache has been purged and refreshed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Mark. What should I test first?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open the Netflix app and launch a 4K title like Our Planet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening Netflix... launching Our Planet... wow, the Ultra HD 4K HDR badge showed up immediately in the top corner!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the playback running smoothly with zero buffering or stuttering?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It started playing in literally two seconds, and the picture quality is breathtaking. The colors and contrast are night and day compared to earlier.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what about Prime Video? Could you test a 4K stream on there as well?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening Prime Video... playing The Rings of Power... HDR10+ badge popped up and it's crystal clear!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Moving the cable to HDMI port one and enabling UHD Color has successfully established full HDCP 2.2 synchronization.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I had no idea the TV port was throttling the resolution all along.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a very common hidden setting on newer 4K screens, Elijah.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the TV box automatically adjust frame rate between 50Hz for live UK TV and 60Hz or 24p for films?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the TV 360 box has Match Frame Rate enabled by default, so it switches refresh rates dynamically without judder.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why motion panning looks so silky smooth now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you also tested BBC iPlayer UHD broadcasts under the beta menu?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I haven't tried iPlayer UHD yet. Does that work through the apps section?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, in BBC iPlayer Settings, enable UHD Trial and you will receive BBC live sport and nature documentaries in 4K HLG.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll definitely turn that on for the tennis tournament this weekend.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if the apps ever freeze in the future, holding the power button on the 360 box for ten seconds performs a soft memory flush.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a really handy shortcut to remember rather than unplugging at the wall.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Mark, you've been brilliant. You explained everything step by step and fixed our 4K picture completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my absolute pleasure helping you today, Elijah. Is there anything else on your TV or broadband that I can check?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, everything is working in stunning 4K now. Thank you so much!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Elijah. Enjoy your 4K movies and have a wonderful week.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Mark, take care. Goodbye.
